prerequisites: Basic knowledge of computer network security problems at the level of popular trade journals (e.g. c't)

learning_outcomes.text: Students will have a comprehensive understanding of the technical aspects of network security.
Students will have recognized that cryptography alone is not enough to solve security problems.
Students will have acquired a comprehensive system understanding for complex IT systems.
Students will prepare for their role in professional life through independent considerations for improving network security.
Students can analyze new problems and develop new solutions.
Students can argumentatively justify the benefits of the solutions they have developed in conversation.
Students will have understood that non-technical factors such as liability issues and resulting costs significantly influence IT security decisions.

syllabus_topics: Security of HTTP (HTTP Authentication, Secure HTTP, Architecture of SSL/TLS)
Transport Layer Security (TLS1.2, versions SSL 2.0 to TLS 1.3)
Attacks on SSL and TLS (BEAST, CRIME, POODLE, Lucky13, Bleichenbacher, DROWN, Heartbleed, Invalid Curve)
The Domain Name System and DNSSEC (factorable keys)
Security of web applications (HTML, URI, XSS, CSRF, SQLi, SSO)
assessment_rules: Credits are awarded upon passing the written exam.
